chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever swears by Allah, let him be truthful; and whoever is not truthful, he is not of Allah. And whoever has an oath sworn to him by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him be pleased with it; and whoever is not pleased, he is not of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.حَلَفَ بِاللَّهِ: To swear/take an oath by Allah — the most binding form of oath in Islamic law
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an epithet of God emphasizing His transcendent power and grandeur
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ: He is not of Allah — a severe expression denoting severance from God's protection/community due to violation of oath
key_terms.فَلْيَرْضَ: Let him be pleased/accept — obligation to accept an oath sworn by Allah as sufficient assurance
key_terms.فَلْيَصْدُقْ: Let him be truthful — imperative form emphasizing obligatory truthfulness when invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about swearing oaths by Allah and the obligation of truthfulness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a two-sided duty regarding oaths taken in the name of Allah: the one who swears must be truthful in what he swears to, and the one for whom an oath is sworn must accept it as sufficient. The severe expression 'he is not of Allah' reflects the gravity of violating the sanctity of God's name — either by lying under oath or by rejecting an oath sworn in God's name as insufficient. This ruling addresses the social context of pledge-making and dispute resolution in early Islamic society, where oaths by God carried the highest legal and moral weight.
